text.p: These are the leading stories in the morning newspaper in the Indian Ocean island of Mauritius on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Opposition parties Mouvement Militant Mauricien (MMM) and Mouvement Socialiste Militant (MSM) top management meeting planned for July 17 now cancelled. MSM said not interested in a joint front if early elections are called on the Indian Ocean island. MSM also not interested in review of the national radio and television policy or electoral system reforms.

-- Initial Public offer of shares in state utility Mauritius Telecoms shares due to open in December 1997. It targets 2.0 billion rupees ($94.29 million) that will be used in setting up a privatisation fund.

-- All Workers Conference (AWC) hostile to Privatisation Fund Bill and Concession Projects Bill. Privatisation Fund Bill aims include making provision for the payment of the proceeds from the sale of state-owned shares into the Privatisation Fund. Concession Projects Bill is to provide for the legal framework for the execution of projects under concession agreements such as Build, Operate and Transfer (BOT), Build, Own and Operate (BOO), Build, Own, Operate and Transfer (BOOT), Design, Build, Finance and Operate (DBFO) and Modernise, Own/Operate and Transfer (MOT).
